param.compression_level.label: Compression level
param.compression_level.tooltip: Compression effort from 0 to 10: higher means a smaller file but a slower conversion. Never alters the geometry.
param.compression_level.help_what: Sets how much effort Draco spends compressing the mesh, from 0 (fastest) to 10 (most compact). It selects the prediction and coding methods; it does not touch coordinate precision.
param.compression_level.help_size: The file shrinks as the level rises. Most of the gain is reached around level 7; levels 8 to 10 squeeze out a few more percent.
param.compression_level.help_quality: None: the resulting geometry is the same at every level. Only encoding and decoding times change.
param.compression_level.help_recommended: 10 for archiving. Lower it only if converting a very large collection feels too slow.
param.compression_level.help_orca: OrcaSlicer always uses the maximum level (10), with no visible setting.
param.position_bits.label: Position quantization bits
param.position_bits.tooltip: Coordinate precision: 0 keeps them as they are; from 1 to 30 they are rounded to a grid (more bits = finer grid).
param.position_bits.help_what: Quantization rounds every coordinate to a regular grid that splits the model's largest dimension into 2^bits − 1 steps. At 0 there is no grid: the original coordinates are kept bit for bit.
param.position_bits.help_size: This is the setting with the largest effect on size. Fewer bits mean a smaller file. The sampled projection measures the real effect on your own files.
param.position_bits.help_quality: Each vertex can move by at most half a step on each axis. Example: 14 bits on a 180 mm model give a step of 0.011 mm. With too few bits, small details collapse and neighbouring vertices merge.
param.position_bits.help_recommended: 0 for a faithful archive. If space matters more, 16 bits keep the deviation under 0.01 mm for a model up to 750 mm; the "Tolerance in mm" profile does this calculation for you.
param.position_bits.help_orca: This is the "Quantization bits" setting of OrcaSlicer's DRC export, whose default is also 0.
param.tolerance_mm.label: Tolerance (mm)
param.tolerance_mm.tooltip: Largest accepted deviation in millimetres: the software picks, for each file, the smallest number of bits that respects it.
param.tolerance_mm.help_what: Instead of fixing a number of bits, you fix the largest deviation a vertex may undergo. For each model, the software works out from its size the smallest number of bits that respects it. When this setting is active it replaces "Position quantization bits".
param.tolerance_mm.help_size: The wider the tolerance, the smaller the files. Small models get fewer bits than large ones, so no space is spent for nothing.
param.tolerance_mm.help_quality: Quality becomes uniform: every model respects the same deviation in millimetres, whatever its size. If even 30 bits are not enough, the model is encoded without quantization.
param.tolerance_mm.help_recommended: 0.001 mm is invisible in print. 0.01 mm matches the usual CAD export tolerance and is still twenty times finer than a 0.2 mm layer.
param.texcoord_bits.label: Texture coordinate bits
param.texcoord_bits.tooltip: Precision of texture coordinates (UV), from 1 to 30 bits; 0 keeps them as they are. No effect on an STL.
param.texcoord_bits.help_what: Rounds texture coordinates (UV) to a grid, as for positions. Only concerns OBJ or PLY files that carry a texture.
param.texcoord_bits.help_size: Moderate effect, and only if the model has texture coordinates. An STL never has any.
param.texcoord_bits.help_quality: With too few bits the texture slides slightly over the surface. The shape of the model is not affected.
param.texcoord_bits.help_recommended: 10 to 12 bits for an ordinary texture. Irrelevant for single-colour 3D printing.
param.normal_bits.label: Normal bits
param.normal_bits.tooltip: Precision of stored normals, from 1 to 30 bits; 0 keeps them as they are. No effect when normals are not stored.
param.normal_bits.help_what: Normals give the orientation of the surface at each vertex and are used for on-screen shading. This setting fixes the precision they are stored with, when they are stored.
param.normal_bits.help_size: Moderate effect, and none as long as "normals" is ticked in the attributes to leave out.
param.normal_bits.help_quality: With too few bits, on-screen shading becomes less smooth. The shape of the model is not affected.
param.normal_bits.help_recommended: 8 bits are enough for display. For 3D printing the simplest choice is not to store normals: a slicer recomputes them.
param.generic_bits.label: Generic attribute bits
param.generic_bits.tooltip: Precision of other per-vertex data, from 1 to 30 bits; 0 keeps them as they are. Rarely useful.
param.generic_bits.help_what: Some files attach per-vertex data that is neither position, normal, texture nor colour. Draco calls these generic attributes; this setting fixes their precision.
param.generic_bits.help_size: Small effect, and none for almost all printing models, which have no such attributes.
param.generic_bits.help_quality: Depends on what the data represents. The shape of the model is not affected.
param.generic_bits.help_recommended: Leave it at 8. This setting only matters for files produced by specialised tools.
param.skip_attributes.label: Attributes to leave out
param.skip_attributes.tooltip: Extra data to leave out: normals, texture coordinates, colours, generic attributes.
param.skip_attributes.help_what: Besides its shape, a 3D file can carry normals, texture coordinates, per-vertex colours or other attributes. Each ticked box leaves the matching data out of the .drc file.
param.skip_attributes.help_size: Every attribute left out makes the file lighter. Normals pay off most: they are heavy and can be recomputed.
param.skip_attributes.help_quality: The shape is never affected. However, data left out is lost: a colour or texture left out will not come back when converting back.
param.skip_attributes.help_recommended: Normals ticked, the rest unticked. An STL only has normals, and they are recomputed when converting back.
param.skip_attributes.help_orca: OrcaSlicer stores the shape only, which amounts to ticking everything.
param.point_cloud.label: Point cloud
param.point_cloud.tooltip: Stores the vertices only, without the triangles. Avoid for 3D printing.
param.point_cloud.help_what: Encodes the file as a plain set of points: the triangles connecting the vertices are dropped. Useful for raw 3D scanner captures.
param.point_cloud.help_size: The file is smaller because the triangles are gone.
param.point_cloud.help_quality: The surface is lost: the result is no longer a solid object and can no longer be sliced or printed.
param.point_cloud.help_recommended: Leave unticked for any model meant for printing.
param.point_cloud.help_orca: No equivalent setting in OrcaSlicer, which expects a mesh.
param.preserve_order.label: Preserve order
param.preserve_order.tooltip: Keeps the original order of vertices and triangles, at the cost of a noticeably larger file.
param.preserve_order.help_what: By default Draco reorders vertices and triangles to compress better. This option prevents it: the decoded file has its vertices and triangles in the same order as the original.
param.preserve_order.help_size: The file is noticeably larger, because the most efficient compression method relies on reordering.
param.preserve_order.help_quality: No effect on the shape. Only the internal order of the data changes.
param.preserve_order.help_recommended: Leave unticked. Order does not matter for printing; it only serves tools that refer to vertices by number.
param.metadata.label: Metadata
param.metadata.tooltip: Keeps the object, group and material names of an OBJ file inside the .drc.
param.metadata.help_what: An OBJ file can name its objects, groups and materials. With this option, Draco's official encoder keeps those names in the .drc instead of dropping them. No effect on an STL, which holds nothing of the kind.
param.metadata.help_size: A few bytes per name, negligible.
param.metadata.help_recommended: Unticked for printing. Tick it if your OBJ files are organised in groups or materials you want to get back.
param.metadata.help_orca: No equivalent setting in OrcaSlicer, which ignores this information when opening.
param.preserve_polygons.label: Preserve polygons
param.preserve_polygons.tooltip: Keeps faces with four or more sides from an OBJ or PLY instead of retaining triangles only.
param.preserve_polygons.help_what: Draco stores triangles. With this option it also records which edges were added to split faces with four or more sides, so those faces can be rebuilt. Only concerns OBJ and PLY; an STL has triangles only.
param.preserve_polygons.help_size: The file grows slightly, by one piece of information per triangle.
param.preserve_polygons.help_quality: No effect on the shape. Only the way faces are split is remembered.
param.preserve_polygons.help_recommended: Leave unticked for printing. Useful only if the model must be reworked in modelling software.
reason.verify_failed: verification of the produced file failed
reason.compiler_obj: compiler object file, not a 3D model
reason.unsafe_zip_entry: archive entry with an unsafe path
reason.replace_forbidden: replacement not allowed for this file type
reason.already_converted: already converted in an earlier run
warning.data_loss: data loss: plates, print settings, colours and object separation are not kept
warning.not_replaceable: the original of this type is never replaced
cli.description: Draco (.drc) converter for 3D models: STL, OBJ, PLY, 3MF and ZIP archives, both ways.
cli.cmd.scan: Lists the 3D files of a file, folder or drive (read-only).
cli.cmd.estimate: Projects the space saved by converting to .drc, without writing anything.
cli.cmd.quality: Measures the quality loss for the given settings, without writing anything.
cli.cmd.encode: Converts a file, folder or drive to .drc.
cli.cmd.decode: Converts .drc files back to binary STL, OBJ or PLY.
cli.cmd.params: Lists the settings, or shows the detailed help of one of them.
cli.arg.paths: Files, folders or drives to process.
cli.arg.param: Identifier of a setting, for example position_bits.
cli.opt.lang: Language of the messages: fr or en.
cli.opt.profile: Starting settings profile; setting options override it.
cli.opt.originals: What happens to originals: keep (default), mirror (mirror folder), replace (recycle bin after verification).
cli.opt.replace_originals: Confirms replace mode: originals go to the recycle bin after verification.
cli.opt.workers: Number of parallel conversions (default: half the cores).
cli.opt.dry_run: Shows the plan without converting anything.
cli.opt.engine: Forces the Draco engine: dracopy (built-in) or reference (official tools).
cli.opt.journal: Batch journal file; reusing it resumes an interrupted batch.
cli.opt.allow_no_gain: Converts even when the produced file is not smaller.
cli.opt.format: Output format: stl (binary, default), obj or ply.
cli.opt.no_zip: Does not open ZIP archives to list their content.
cli.opt.sample: Refined projection: actually encodes a sample of files.
cli.opt.per_class: Files sampled per kind and size class (default 12).
cli.opt.seed: Random seed, for a reproducible result.
cli.opt.curve: Writes to this CSV file the size and deviation obtained from 8 to 29 bits.
cli.opt.max_files: On a folder, number of files measured (default 10).
cli.opt.skip_values: Comma-separated values among: {choices}; "none" to keep everything.
cli.estimate.no_gain: Files with no gain in the sample
cli.quality.marks: For reference: layer {layer} mm, nozzle {nozzle} mm, CAD tolerance {cad} mm
cli.batch.paused: Batch paused: {reason}. Run the same command again to resume.
cli.batch.free_space: Warning: not enough free space on the destination for the projected size ({needed}).
cli.error.replace: Replace mode sends originals to the recycle bin: add --replace-originals to confirm.
cli.error.unknown_param: Unknown setting: {name}. Run "dracoconv params" for the list.
